subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: Should this be fixed as one maintainer-owned Codex lifecycle repair, or split into separate parser, shared-client cleanup, and fallback transcript issues before implementation?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans Codex app-server lifecycle ownership and cross-provider transcript semantics, and the issue already carries maintainer/product-review labels plus no-new-fix-pr routing.

options.title: Keep One Codex Lifecycle Repair
options.body: Treat the parser, shared-client cleanup, and failover transcript behavior as one coupled P1 repair with live proof before implementation.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Issues
options.body: Create separate canonical work items for rollout parsing/noise, one-shot shared-client retirement, and fallback transcript continuity, then keep this issue as the umbrella until they land.

options.title: Accept Partial Fix For Now
options.body: Close only the missing-file warning path as solved and leave the remaining lifecycle risks to future reports, which does not match the current evidence.

recommendation.title: Keep One Codex Lifecycle Repair
recommendation.body: Treat the parser, shared-client cleanup, and failover transcript behavior as one coupled P1 repair with live proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the related missing-history fix and have the most recent maintainer-side context on what was intentionally scoped out.
